guide.what: An adjective (adjetivo) describes a noun: what it is like, its color, size, origin or state. In Spanish, adjectives change their ending to match the noun.

rules.d: The adjective takes the same gender (masculine/feminine) and number (singular/plural) as the noun. Words in -o change to -a; words in -e or a consonant usually have one form for both genders. Add -s or -es for plural.
rules.ex: un carro rojo, una casa roja, dos casas grandes
rules.exEn: a red car, a red house, two big houses

rules.d: Most adjectives, and always colors and nationalities, go after the noun. This is the opposite of English.
rules.ex: Tengo un celular nuevo y una computadora blanca.
rules.exEn: I have a new phone and a white computer.

rules.d: Some adjectives lose their ending before a masculine singular noun: bueno → buen, malo → mal, primero → primer, tercero → tercer, alguno → algún, ninguno → ningún. Grande becomes gran before any singular noun.
rules.ex: Es un buen día, pero hay un gran problema: no tengo ningún plan.
rules.exEn: It's a nice day, but there's a big problem: I have no plan.

rules.d: A few adjectives mean one thing after the noun and another before it: un hombre grande (big) / un gran hombre (great); un amigo viejo (elderly) / un viejo amigo (long-time); una familia pobre (no money) / ¡pobre familia! (unlucky); un carro nuevo (brand-new) / un nuevo carro (another one).
rules.ex: Es un viejo amigo, pero no es un hombre viejo.
rules.exEn: He's an old friend, but he's not an old man.

rules.d: Use ser for what something is like by nature (character, origin, looks). Use estar for a state or how something is right now. Some adjectives change meaning: ser listo (smart) / estar listo (ready); ser aburrido (boring) / estar aburrido (bored); ser rico (rich) / estar rico (tasty).
rules.ex: Mi hermano es aburrido, pero hoy yo estoy aburrida.
rules.exEn: My brother is boring, but today I'm bored.

rules.t: Comparing: más… que, menos… que, tan… como
rules.d: Use más or menos + adjective + que to compare, and tan + adjective + como for equal. Four special forms: mejor (better), peor (worse), mayor (older), menor (younger).
rules.ex: Mi casa es más pequeña que la tuya, pero es tan bonita como la de Ana.
rules.exEn: My house is smaller than yours, but it's as pretty as Ana's.

rules.d: For the most, use el/la/los/las + más + adjective (+ de). For very, very, add -ísimo to the adjective: caro → carísimo, fácil → facilísimo.
rules.ex: Es el restaurante más caro de la ciudad; la comida está riquísima.
rules.exEn: It's the most expensive restaurant in the city; the food is super tasty.

rules.d: Put lo before a masculine singular adjective to talk about an idea: lo bueno (the good thing), lo malo (the bad part), lo importante (what matters).
rules.ex: Lo bueno de Panamá es que no hace frío.
rules.exEn: The good thing about Panama is that it's never cold.

mistakes.why: The adjective must match the feminine noun.
Bored is a state, so use estar; soy aburrido means I'm boring.

mistakes.wrong: Es más bueno que el otro.
mistakes.why: For quality use mejor and peor, not más bueno or más malo.
Bueno shortens to buen before a masculine singular noun.

mistakes.wrong: Estoy muy excitado por el viaje.
mistakes.right: Estoy muy emocionado por el viaje.
mistakes.why: Excitado sounds sexual; excited is emocionado.

items.use: Before a masculine singular noun it shortens to buen: un buen día. Ser bueno = be good (by nature); estar bueno = taste good (food).
items.ex: Este restaurante tiene muy buena comida.
items.exEn: This restaurant has really good food.
items.latam: Bueno is also how people answer the phone in Mexico; in Panama people usually say aló.

items.use: Goes before the noun and agrees: mucha gente, muchos carros. Never say muy mucho.
items.ex: Hay mucha gente en el súper hoy.
items.exEn: There are a lot of people at the supermarket today.

items.use: Shortens to mal before a masculine singular noun: un mal momento. Ser malo = be bad or mean; estar malo = be sick or taste bad.
items.ex: Hoy hace mal tiempo, mejor nos quedamos en casa.
items.exEn: The weather is bad today; we'd better stay home.

items.use: Before the noun it means same: el mismo carro. After a noun or pronoun it means -self: yo mismo (I myself).
items.ex: Vivimos en el mismo edificio desde hace años.
items.exEn: We've lived in the same building for years.
items.latam: Ahorita mismo means right now in Panama and much of Latin America.

items.use: Before the noun and agrees: poca agua, pocos amigos. Un poco de = a little bit of.
items.ex: Tengo poco tiempo esta semana.
items.exEn: I have little time this week.

items.use: After the noun = brand-new (un carro nuevo). Before the noun = another, different one (un nuevo carro, maybe used).
items.ex: Me compré un celular nuevo ayer.
items.exEn: I bought myself a new phone yesterday.

items.use: Comparative of bueno: mejor que (better than). With el/la/los/las it means the best. Never say más bueno for quality.
items.ex: Este plan es mejor que el otro.
items.exEn: This plan is better than the other one.

items.use: Shortens to primer before a masculine singular noun: el primer día. The feminine stays primera: la primera vez.
items.ex: Es mi primer año en Panamá.
items.exEn: It's my first year in Panama.

items.use: After the noun it means big: una casa grande. Before any singular noun it shortens to gran and means great: un gran hombre.
items.ex: Panamá es una gran ciudad para vivir.
items.exEn: Panama is a great city to live in.

items.use: After the noun = old: un carro viejo. Before the noun = long-time: un viejo amigo (an old friend, not an elderly one).
items.ex: Mi abuelo tiene un carro muy viejo.
items.exEn: My grandpa has a very old car.
items.latam: Calling people viejo can sound rude; use mayor for elderly people.

items.use: Ser seguro = be safe (a place, a thing). Estar seguro = be sure (a person). Estoy seguro de que viene.
items.ex: ¿Estás segura de que la tienda abre hoy?
items.exEn: Are you sure the store opens today?
items.latam: Seguro also means insurance as a noun: el seguro del carro.

items.use: After a color it means light: azul claro. ¡Claro! alone means of course.
items.ex: Explícalo de una forma clara, por favor.
items.exEn: Explain it clearly, please.

items.use: Usually before the noun: la última vez. Por último = finally.
items.ex: Es el último bus de la noche.
items.exEn: It's the last bus of the night.

items.use: Estar solo = be alone. Write it without an accent today, also when it means only (adverb).
items.ex: No me gusta comer solo.
items.exEn: I don't like to eat alone.

items.use: Usually goes after the noun. For age it can mean young: mi hermano pequeño (my little brother).
items.ex: Vivimos en un apartamento pequeño cerca del mar.
items.exEn: We live in a small apartment near the sea.
items.latam: In Latin America chico and chiquito are very common for small.

items.use: Before the noun = only: el único problema. After the noun = unique: una oportunidad única.
items.ex: Eres la única persona que me entiende.
items.exEn: You're the only person who understands me.

items.use: Use estar: Está muerto. Estar muerto de + noun = be dying of: muerto de hambre.
items.ex: Estoy muerto de cansancio.
items.exEn: I'm dead tired.

items.use: After ser = true: Es cierto. Before the noun = a certain, some: cierta persona. No use un before it: cierto día, not un cierto día.
items.ex: Es cierto que el tráfico está peor este año.
items.exEn: It's true that traffic is worse this year.

items.use: Agrees with the noun: el segundo piso, la segunda calle. Also a noun: un segundo (a second).
items.ex: Vivo en el segundo piso.
items.exEn: I live on the second floor.

items.use: Ser serio = be serious by nature. Estar serio = look serious right now. En serio = seriously, really.
items.ex: ¿Hablas en serio?
items.exEn: Are you serious?

items.use: Goes before the noun and agrees with it: mi propia casa. After the noun it can mean typical: propio de (typical of).
items.ex: Quiero tener mi propio negocio.
items.exEn: I want to have my own business.

items.use: Agrees with the people: Vamos juntos, vamos juntas. Junto a = next to (does not change).
items.ex: Siempre almorzamos juntos los viernes.
items.exEn: We always have lunch together on Fridays.

items.use: Comparative of grande for age and importance: mayor que (older than). Una persona mayor = an elderly person. El mayor = the oldest.
items.ex: Mi hermana es mayor que yo.
items.exEn: My sister is older than me.

items.use: Same form for masculine and feminine. Es importante + infinitive: Es importante llegar temprano.
items.ex: Tengo una reunión importante mañana.
items.exEn: I have an important meeting tomorrow.

items.use: Ser bajo = be short (height). Also low: precios bajos. Speak quietly = en voz baja.
items.ex: Mi mamá es baja y tiene el pelo rizado.
items.exEn: My mom is short and has curly hair.
items.latam: Chaparro (short person) is common in Mexico, not in Panama.

items.use: Ser alto = be tall. For sound it means loud: en voz alta (out loud).
items.ex: Mi novio es muy alto.
items.exEn: My boyfriend is very tall.

items.use: Agrees as an adjective: una comida rápida. As an adverb (quickly) it stays rápido.
items.ex: El metro es más rápido que el bus.
items.exEn: The metro is faster than the bus.

items.use: Same form for both genders; plural jóvenes (note the accent). Also a noun: los jóvenes.
items.ex: Mi jefe es muy joven.
items.exEn: My boss is very young.

items.use: Same form for both genders; plural felices. Used with ser and estar: Estoy feliz hoy.
items.ex: Estamos muy felices con la noticia.
items.exEn: We're very happy about the news.

items.use: Es posible que + subjunctive: Es posible que llueva. Lo antes posible = as soon as possible.
items.ex: ¿Es posible cambiar la cita para el lunes?
items.exEn: Is it possible to change the appointment to Monday?

items.use: Same form for both genders; plural difíciles. Es difícil + infinitive: Es difícil encontrar parking.
items.ex: El examen fue más difícil de lo que pensaba.
items.exEn: The exam was harder than I thought.

items.use: False friend: largo means long, not large. Large is grande.
items.ex: Tiene el pelo largo y negro.
items.exEn: She has long black hair.

items.use: Igual que = the same as. Same form for both genders; plural iguales.
items.ex: Tu celular es igual que el mío.
items.exEn: Your phone is the same as mine.
items.latam: Igual is also used as an adverb meaning anyway: Igual voy a ir.

items.use: Estar vivo = be alive. Ser vivo = be sharp or clever. Colores vivos = bright colors.
items.ex: Por suerte el perro está vivo.
items.exEn: Luckily the dog is alive.
items.latam: In Panama and Latin America ser vivo often means clever or a bit sly.

items.use: Agrees with the noun. Salir caro = turn out expensive.
items.ex: La vida en la ciudad es cara.
items.exEn: Life in the city is expensive.

items.use: Ser justo = be fair. Estar justo = fit tight. Justo as adverb = just, exactly.
items.ex: No es justo que siempre pague yo.
items.exEn: It's not fair that I always pay.

items.use: Usually before the noun and agrees in number: suficientes sillas. Same form for both genders.
items.ex: No tenemos suficiente tiempo.
items.exEn: We don't have enough time.

items.use: Goes before the noun for the next in the future: la próxima semana. Hasta la próxima = see you next time.
items.ex: Nos vemos la próxima semana.
items.exEn: See you next week.

items.use: Estar tranquilo = feel calm. Ser tranquilo = be a calm person or quiet place. ¡Tranquilo! = relax.
items.ex: Tranquila, todo va a salir bien.
items.exEn: Relax, everything is going to be fine.
items.latam: In Panama you often hear tranquilo or tranqui to mean relax, no problem.

items.use: Same form for both genders. It also means heavy (rain) or loud: una lluvia fuerte, música fuerte.
items.ex: Anoche cayó un aguacero muy fuerte.
items.exEn: Last night there was a very heavy downpour.
items.latam: Aguacero (heavy rain) is the everyday word in Panama.

items.use: Agrees with the noun: una tienda barata. As an adverb it stays barato: Compré barato.
items.ex: Encontré un vuelo barato a Bogotá.
items.exEn: I found a cheap flight to Bogotá.

items.use: Estar listo = be ready. Ser listo = be smart. ¿Estás lista? = Are you ready?
items.ex: Ya estoy listo, podemos salir.
items.exEn: I'm ready now, we can leave.

items.use: For things: el agua está fría. For weather use hace frío; for people tengo frío.
items.ex: Quiero una cerveza bien fría.
items.exEn: I want a really cold beer.

items.use: Colors go after the noun and agree: camisa blanca, zapatos blancos.
items.ex: Necesito una camisa blanca para la entrevista.
items.exEn: I need a white shirt for the interview.

items.use: Goes after the noun and agrees: frijoles negros. Café negro = black coffee.
items.ex: Me gusta el café negro, sin azúcar.
items.exEn: I like black coffee, without sugar.

items.use: After the noun = different: una idea diferente. Before a plural noun = various: diferentes opciones. Diferente de or a = different from.
items.ex: Cada día es diferente en este trabajo.
items.exEn: Every day is different in this job.

items.use: Same form for both genders. It means real (true) and also royal: la familia real.
items.ex: Es una historia real.
items.exEn: It's a true story.

items.use: More formal than raro. As a verb, extraño means I miss: Te extraño.
items.ex: Escuché un ruido extraño en la cocina.
items.exEn: I heard a strange noise in the kitchen.

items.use: Same form for both genders; plural especiales. En especial = especially.
items.ex: Hoy es un día especial para mi familia.
items.exEn: Today is a special day for my family.

items.use: Estar enfermo = be sick now. Ser enfermo = have a chronic illness.
items.ex: Mi hijo está enfermo y no fue a la escuela.
items.exEn: My son is sick and didn't go to school.

items.use: Hard to touch or hard to bear: un trabajo duro. Ser duro = be strict.
items.ex: Fue una semana muy dura.
items.exEn: It was a very tough week.

items.use: Same form for both genders; plural fáciles. Es fácil de + infinitive: Es fácil de usar.
items.ex: Esta receta es muy fácil.
items.exEn: This recipe is very easy.

items.use: Ser rico = be rich. Estar rico = taste delicious: La sopa está rica.
items.ex: ¡Qué rico está este sancocho!
items.exEn: This sancocho is so delicious!
items.latam: Rico for tasty food is everyday Panamanian Spanish.

items.use: Nationalities are not capitalized in Spanish. Add -a for the feminine: española.
items.ex: Mi profesora es española, de Madrid.
items.exEn: My teacher is Spanish, from Madrid.

items.use: Means free as in not busy or not occupied. Free as in no cost is gratis.
items.ex: ¿Tienes tiempo libre este fin de semana?
items.exEn: Do you have free time this weekend?

items.use: Same form for both genders. Usually with el/la: al día siguiente (the next day).
items.ex: Al día siguiente fuimos a la playa.
items.exEn: The next day we went to the beach.

items.use: Agrees with the noun: la respuesta correcta. ¡Correcto! = That's right.
items.ex: Marca la respuesta correcta.
items.exEn: Mark the correct answer.

items.use: Goes after the noun and agrees: luz roja, carros rojos.
items.ex: El semáforo está en rojo.
items.exEn: The traffic light is red.

items.use: Same form for both genders; plural azules. Azul claro = light blue, azul oscuro = dark blue.
items.ex: El mar está muy azul hoy.
items.exEn: The sea is very blue today.

items.use: Stronger than bonito. It can go before the noun for style: un hermoso día.
items.ex: Panamá tiene playas hermosas.
items.exEn: Panama has beautiful beaches.

items.use: For things and people. Usually after the noun: una casa bonita.
items.ex: Tienes una sonrisa muy bonita.
items.exEn: You have a very pretty smile.

items.use: Comparative of malo: peor que (worse than). With el/la = the worst. Never say más malo for quality.
items.ex: El tráfico hoy está peor que ayer.
items.exEn: Traffic today is worse than yesterday.

items.use: Es necesario + infinitive, or es necesario que + subjunctive.
items.ex: No es necesario traer nada.
items.exEn: It's not necessary to bring anything.

items.use: For people who are pleasant and friendly. It does not mean sympathetic (that is comprensivo).
items.ex: Tus amigos son muy simpáticos.
items.exEn: Your friends are really nice.
items.latam: In Latin America people use simpático a lot; caer bien is also common: Me cae bien.

items.use: Agrees with the noun. ¡Perfecto! alone means great or that works.
items.ex: El clima está perfecto para ir a la playa.
items.exEn: The weather is perfect for going to the beach.

items.use: Usually means weird, not rare. Qué raro = how strange.
items.ex: Qué raro, Ana nunca llega tarde.
items.exEn: How strange, Ana is never late.

items.use: Use estar: La nevera está vacía. Note the accent on í.
items.ex: La nevera está vacía, hay que ir al súper.
items.exEn: The fridge is empty; we need to go to the supermarket.

items.use: Lowercase. Agrees: la comida panameña, los panameños.
items.ex: Mi esposa es panameña, de Chitré.
items.exEn: My wife is Panamanian, from Chitré.

items.use: Estar cansado = be tired. Ser cansado = be tiring (a job, a trip).
items.ex: Llego muy cansado del trabajo.
items.exEn: I get home very tired from work.

items.use: Same form for both genders. Estar triste = feel sad; ser triste = be a sad thing.
items.ex: Estoy triste porque mi amiga se fue.
items.exEn: I'm sad because my friend left.

items.use: Before the noun it stresses real: un verdadero amigo. Verdadero o falso = true or false.
items.ex: Ella es una verdadera amiga.
items.exEn: She is a true friend.

items.use: Same form for both genders. Estar verde = be unripe or inexperienced.
items.ex: Estos mangos todavía están verdes.
items.exEn: These mangoes are still green.
items.latam: In Panama mango verde with salt is a popular snack.

items.use: Use estar: El bus está lleno. Lleno de = full of.
items.ex: El restaurante estaba lleno de gente.
items.exEn: The restaurant was full of people.

items.use: Always with estar: Estoy contento con el trabajo.
items.ex: Estoy muy contenta con mi nuevo trabajo.
items.exEn: I'm very happy with my new job.

items.use: After the noun = poor (no money): una familia pobre. Before the noun = unfortunate: ¡Pobre chico! (poor guy).
items.ex: El pobre perro estaba mojado y con hambre.
items.exEn: The poor dog was wet and hungry.

items.use: Very common in Latin America for people, things and even kind actions: Qué lindo de tu parte.
items.ex: ¡Qué linda está la playa hoy!
items.exEn: The beach looks so lovely today!
items.latam: Lindo is much more common in Latin America than in Spain.

items.use: Mild word; fine between friends. Ser tonto = be silly; estar tonto = act silly.
items.ex: No seas tonto, claro que te ayudo.
items.exEn: Don't be silly, of course I'll help you.

items.use: Estar abierto = be open now. Ser abierto = be open-minded (a person).
items.ex: ¿El banco está abierto los sábados?
items.exEn: Is the bank open on Saturdays?

items.use: Accent only on the masculine singular: inglés, inglesa, ingleses. Also the language: el inglés.
items.ex: Ella da clases de inglés.
items.exEn: She teaches English classes.

items.use: For looks and also bad situations: Está feo el tiempo (the weather is nasty).
items.ex: El edificio es feo, pero el apartamento es lindo.
items.exEn: The building is ugly, but the apartment is nice.
items.latam: In Panama está feo is often used for a bad or risky situation.

items.use: Shortens to tercer before a masculine singular noun: el tercer piso. Feminine stays: la tercera vez.
items.ex: La oficina está en el tercer piso.
items.exEn: The office is on the third floor.

items.use: Ser capaz de + infinitive = be able to. Plural capaces.
items.ex: Eres capaz de hacerlo solo.
items.exEn: You're capable of doing it on your own.
items.latam: In Latin America capaz que means maybe: Capaz que llueve.

items.use: Same form for both genders. Es increíble que + subjunctive.
items.ex: La vista desde el Cerro Ancón es increíble.
items.exEn: The view from Ancon Hill is amazing.

items.use: Ser divertido = be fun. Do not confuse with estar divertido (amused), which is rare.
items.ex: La fiesta fue muy divertida.
items.exEn: The party was a lot of fun.

items.use: Same form for both genders. Usually after the noun: la calle principal, el plato principal.
items.ex: El problema principal es el tráfico.
items.exEn: The main problem is traffic.

items.use: After the noun = very old: un edificio antiguo. Before the noun = former: mi antiguo jefe.
items.ex: Casco Antiguo es la parte más antigua de la ciudad.
items.exEn: Casco Antiguo is the oldest part of the city.

items.use: Ser aburrido = be boring. Estar aburrido = be bored. Mixing them changes the meaning.
items.ex: Estoy aburrido, ¿vamos al cine?
items.exEn: I'm bored, shall we go to the movies?

items.use: Same form for both genders; plural normales. Es normal que + subjunctive.
items.ex: Es normal sentirse nervioso antes del examen.
items.exEn: It's normal to feel nervous before the exam.

items.use: Agrees with the noun. Por completo = completely. Tiempo completo = full time.
items.ex: Trabajo a tiempo completo.
items.exEn: I work full time.

items.use: Agrees with the noun. Stronger than bueno or lindo.
items.ex: Pasamos un fin de semana maravilloso en Boquete.
items.exEn: We had a wonderful weekend in Boquete.

items.use: Same form for both genders. Es imposible + infinitive.
items.ex: Es imposible encontrar estacionamiento aquí.
items.exEn: It's impossible to find parking here.

items.use: Same form for both genders; plural comunes (no accent). En común = in common.
items.ex: Tenemos muchas cosas en común.
items.exEn: We have a lot in common.

items.use: Same form for both genders. Usually after the noun: la semana anterior.
items.ex: Mi trabajo anterior era más lejos.
items.exEn: My previous job was farther away.

items.use: Goes after the noun and agrees: flores amarillas.
items.ex: Los taxis en Panamá son amarillos.
items.exEn: Taxis in Panama are yellow.

items.use: Same form for both genders. Ser interesante = be interesting; estar interesado = be interested.
items.ex: Fue una conversación muy interesante.
items.exEn: It was a very interesting conversation.

items.use: Comparative for age: menor que (younger than). El menor = the youngest. Menor de edad = a minor.
items.ex: Mi hermano menor vive en Colón.
items.exEn: My younger brother lives in Colón.

items.use: Use ser for places and things: Esa calle es peligrosa de noche.
items.ex: Es peligroso manejar con tanta lluvia.
items.exEn: It's dangerous to drive in so much rain.

items.use: Can sound rude about people; gordito sounds softer. Also used as a term of affection.
items.ex: Este libro es muy gordo.
items.exEn: This book is very thick.

items.use: Same form for both genders. Use ser: Es muy inteligente.
items.ex: Mi hija es muy inteligente.
items.exEn: My daughter is very smart.

items.use: Use estar: Está enojada conmigo. Enojado con = angry at.
items.ex: Mi jefe está enojado conmigo.
items.exEn: My boss is angry with me.
items.latam: Spain says enfadado; Latin America says enojado. In Panama you also hear bravo: Está bravo.

items.use: For length and time: pelo corto, un viaje corto. For a short person use bajo.
items.ex: Fue un viaje corto, solo dos días.
items.exEn: It was a short trip, only two days.

items.use: Same form for both genders. It can go before the noun for emphasis: un terrible error.
items.ex: Hoy tuve un día terrible.
items.exEn: I had an awful day today.

items.use: Estar cerrado = be closed. Ser cerrado = be closed-minded.
items.ex: La farmacia ya está cerrada.
items.exEn: The pharmacy is already closed.

items.use: Polite word for slim people. Flaco is more casual.
items.ex: Está más delgada después de ir al gimnasio.
items.exEn: She's slimmer since going to the gym.
items.latam: Flaco is the everyday word in Latin America, often used as a nickname.

items.use: Estar limpio = be clean now. Agrees: la casa está limpia.
items.ex: La cocina ya está limpia.
items.exEn: The kitchen is clean now.

items.use: Can mean from the Americas in general. For the US, estadounidense is more exact.
items.ex: El continente americano es muy grande.
items.exEn: The American continent is very big.
items.latam: Many Latin Americans see americano as all the Americas; say estadounidense or gringo (casual) for the US.

items.use: Use estar: Estoy preocupado por ti.
items.ex: Estoy preocupada por el examen.
items.exEn: I'm worried about the exam.

items.use: Same form for both genders. Very common in speech: ¡Qué horrible!
items.ex: El tranque estuvo horrible esta mañana.
items.exEn: The traffic jam was awful this morning.
items.latam: Tranque is the Panamanian word for traffic jam.

items.use: Accent only on the masculine singular: alemán, alemana, alemanes.
items.ex: Mi vecino es alemán.
items.exEn: My neighbor is German.

items.use: Same form for both genders; plural grises.
items.ex: El cielo está gris, va a llover.
items.exEn: The sky is gray; it's going to rain.

items.use: Ser alegre = be a cheerful person. Estar alegre = feel happy now.
items.ex: Mi abuela es una persona muy alegre.
items.exEn: My grandmother is a very cheerful person.

items.use: After a color = dark: verde oscuro. Also for places: una calle oscura.
items.ex: Prefiero los colores oscuros.
items.exEn: I prefer dark colors.

items.use: Means funny or amusing, not gracious.
items.ex: Mi tío es muy gracioso, siempre cuenta chistes.
items.exEn: My uncle is very funny; he always tells jokes.

items.use: Ser responsable = be a responsible person. Ser responsable de = be in charge of.
items.ex: Ella es muy responsable con su trabajo.
items.exEn: She is very responsible with her work.

items.use: Same form for both genders. Use ser: Es muy amable. Muy amable = how kind of you.
items.ex: La señora del banco fue muy amable.
items.exEn: The lady at the bank was very kind.

items.use: Use estar: Los platos están sucios.
items.ex: Tu camisa está sucia.
items.exEn: Your shirt is dirty.

items.use: False friend: actual means current, not actual. Actually = en realidad.
items.ex: El precio actual es de veinte dólares.
items.exEn: The current price is twenty dollars.

items.use: Accent only on the masculine singular: francés, francesa, franceses.
items.ex: Estoy aprendiendo francés también.
items.exEn: I'm learning French too.

items.use: Estar nervioso = feel nervous now. Ser nervioso = be a nervous person.
items.ex: Siempre me pongo nervioso antes de hablar en público.
items.exEn: I always get nervous before speaking in public.

items.use: For things, not weather: el café está caliente. For weather use hace calor; for people tengo calor.
items.ex: Cuidado, la sopa está muy caliente.
items.exEn: Careful, the soup is very hot.
items.latam: Avoid estoy caliente for I'm hot; it sounds sexual. Say tengo calor.

items.use: Same form for both genders. Also for people: Es muy dulce. As a noun: un dulce (a candy).
items.ex: Este café está muy dulce.
items.exEn: This coffee is very sweet.

items.use: For wrong facts and fake things: un billete falso. Also two-faced (a person).
items.ex: Ese billete de veinte es falso.
items.exEn: That twenty-dollar bill is fake.

items.use: Same form for both genders. Already strong, so muy enorme sounds odd.
items.ex: El centro comercial es enorme.
items.exEn: The mall is huge.

items.use: For hair and people: Es rubia. Agrees with the person.
items.ex: Su hija es rubia y tiene los ojos azules.
items.exEn: Her daughter is blonde and has blue eyes.

items.use: Same form for both genders. Used alone to say great.
items.ex: El servicio fue excelente.
items.exEn: The service was excellent.

items.use: Can describe dark hair or tanned or darker skin. Agrees with the person.
items.ex: Mi novio es alto y moreno.
items.exEn: My boyfriend is tall and dark-haired.

items.use: Estar enamorado de = be in love with (use de, not con).
items.ex: Está enamorado de su compañera de clase.
items.exEn: He's in love with his classmate.

items.use: Ser guapo = be good-looking. Estar guapo = look good today.
items.ex: Tu hermano es muy guapo.
items.exEn: Your brother is very handsome.
items.latam: In Latin America guapo is used less than in Spain; lindo and bonito are more common. In parts of the Caribbean guapo can mean tough or brave.

items.use: Estar orgulloso de = be proud of. Ser orgulloso = be arrogant.
items.ex: Estoy muy orgulloso de ti.
items.exEn: I'm very proud of you.

items.use: Use estar: Estoy ocupado. Also taken (a seat or bathroom).
items.ex: Hoy estoy muy ocupada, te llamo mañana.
items.exEn: I'm very busy today; I'll call you tomorrow.

items.use: Ser famoso por = be famous for.
items.ex: Panamá es famoso por su canal.
items.exEn: Panama is famous for its canal.

items.use: Agrees with the noun: mi comida favorita, mis canciones favoritas.
items.ex: El arroz con pollo es mi comida favorita.
items.exEn: Chicken and rice is my favorite food.

items.use: Use estar: Estoy emocionado por el viaje. Excited is not excitado (that is sexual).
items.ex: Estamos emocionados por el viaje a Bocas.
items.exEn: We're excited about the trip to Bocas.

items.use: Use estar: Estoy asustado. Also tener miedo.
items.ex: El niño estaba asustado por la tormenta.
items.exEn: The boy was scared of the storm.

items.use: Add -a for the feminine: trabajadora. Also a noun: un trabajador (a worker).
items.ex: Mi papá es muy trabajador.
items.exEn: My dad is very hard-working.

items.use: Agrees with the noun: el hospital más cercano. For close family: un pariente cercano.
items.ex: ¿Dónde está la farmacia más cercana?
items.exEn: Where is the nearest pharmacy?

items.use: Same form for both genders; plural débiles. Estar débil = feel weak right now.
items.ex: Todavía me siento débil después de la gripe.
items.exEn: I still feel weak after the flu.

items.use: Agrees with the noun. Usually after it: un edificio moderno.
items.ex: Viven en un edificio muy moderno.
items.exEn: They live in a very modern building.

items.use: Agrees with the noun: una blusa rosada.
items.ex: Compró un vestido rosado para la fiesta.
items.exEn: She bought a pink dress for the party.
items.latam: Rosado is the usual word in Panama; Spain prefers rosa, which does not change.

items.use: For food = fresh: pescado fresco. For weather = cool: Hace fresco.
items.ex: Compramos pescado fresco en el mercado.
items.exEn: We bought fresh fish at the market.

items.use: For easy or plain things and modest people: una persona sencilla.
items.ex: Es una receta sencilla.
items.exEn: It's a simple recipe.
items.latam: In Panama sencillo is also a noun meaning small change (coins).

items.use: Agrees with the noun. Estar complicado = be tricky right now.
items.ex: El trámite es un poco complicado.
items.exEn: The paperwork is a bit complicated.

items.use: Same form for both genders; plural marrones (no accent).
items.ex: Tengo los ojos marrones.
items.exEn: I have brown eyes.
items.latam: In Panama and much of Latin America café is more common: zapatos café.

items.use: Lowercase, agrees with the noun: comida mexicana.
items.ex: Me encanta la comida mexicana.
items.exEn: I love Mexican food.

items.use: False friend: it means polite, not educated. Educated = culto or con estudios.
items.ex: Tus hijos son muy educados.
items.exEn: Your kids are very polite.

items.use: For things and people: Estoy cómodo. Estos zapatos son cómodos.
items.ex: Este sofá es muy cómodo.
items.exEn: This sofa is very comfortable.

items.use: Ser tímido = be a shy person. Note the accent on the first í.
items.ex: Mi hijo es tímido con la gente nueva.
items.exEn: My son is shy with new people.

items.use: Agrees with the noun: un internet lento. The adverb is lento or lentamente.
items.ex: El internet está muy lento hoy.
items.exEn: The internet is really slow today.

items.use: Same form for both genders. Exact word for people from the United States.
items.ex: Hay muchos jubilados estadounidenses en Panamá.
items.exEn: There are many American retirees in Panama.

items.use: For food and people: comida sana. Estar sano = be in good health.
items.ex: Trato de comer más sano.
items.exEn: I try to eat healthier.
